test: Texas DPS Class C Knowledge Exam (learner license / first driver license)
edition: Based on the Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7), Texas Department of Public Safety, Driver License Division, revised January 2026 (current edition as of October 2026)

exam.rules: Every first-time (original) Texas applicant must pass the Class C knowledge exam; you need 70 percent or better (21 of 30). Teens 15–17 usually take it as part of the classroom phase of a driver education course—many TDLR-approved online, school, and parent-taught providers give the test inside the course—and otherwise take it at a DPS driver license office when applying for the learner license. Applicants under 25 must complete driver education (18–24: a 6-hour adult course, which may also include the knowledge test). There is no separately scored road-sign section: signs, signals, and rules are mixed in one test. Adults 18 and older who surrender a valid out-of-state license do not take the knowledge or driving exams. If you fail, your application stays open for 90 days; after 90 days or three failed exams you must re-apply and pay the fee again. All in-person DPS services are by appointment. The Impact Texas Drivers (ITD) video course is required before the driving test (certificate dated within 90 days), not before the knowledge exam. DPS states the 70% pass mark; the 30-question count comes from driver-education providers and test-prep sources because DPS does not publish it.

questions.q: What is the youngest age at which a Texas teen who has completed the classroom part of driver education can get a learner license?
questions.explain: A learner license (instruction permit) can be issued from age 15 once the classroom portion of driver education, the vision exam and the knowledge exam are complete.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Learner License (Instruction Permit)'

questions.q: Who may supervise a driver holding a Texas learner license?
options: A licensed driver at least 21 years old with at least one year of driving experience, seated beside the learner
Any licensed passenger, as long as there are no other passengers under 21
Any licensed driver at least 18 years old, seated anywhere in the vehicle
A licensed driver at least 25 years old with at least five years of driving experience, seated in the back
questions.explain: The supervising driver must be 21 or older, have at least one year of driving experience, occupy the seat beside the learner, and be alert and sober.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Learner License (Instruction Permit)'

questions.q: A learner license issued to a person under 18 expires:
options: Six months after it is issued
One year after it is issued
questions.explain: A Texas learner license issued to a minor expires on the minor's 18th birthday.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Learner License (Instruction Permit)'

questions.q: Under the Graduated Driver License program, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner or hardship license before getting a provisional license?
questions.explain: Phase One requires holding a learner, hardship, or combination license for a minimum of six months before a provisional license is issued.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Graduated Driver License (GDL)'

questions.q: If a teen's learner license is suspended during Phase One of the GDL program, what happens to the required six-month holding period?
options: It is extended by the number of days the license was suspended
It is waived once the suspension ends
questions.explain: Because the license is invalid while suspended, the six-month period is extended by the length of the suspension.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Graduated Driver License (GDL)'

questions.q: A 16-year-old with a provisional license may NOT drive with:
options: More than three passengers of any age
Any passenger who is a family member
More than one passenger under 21 who is not a family member
questions.explain: During Phase Two, a provisional driver may not carry more than one passenger under 21 who is not a family member.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Graduated Driver License (GDL)'

questions.q: During which hours is a Texas provisional (Phase Two) driver generally not allowed to drive?
questions.explain: Provisional drivers may not drive between midnight and 5:00 a.m. unless it is necessary for work, a school-related activity, or a medical emergency.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Graduated Driver License (GDL)'

questions.q: Which reason allows a provisional driver to drive between midnight and 5:00 a.m.?
options: Practicing for the driving exam with friends
Driving friends home from a party
questions.explain: The late-night restriction has exceptions only for work, school-related activities, and medical emergencies.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Graduated Driver License (GDL)'

questions.q: What does Texas law say about drivers under 18 using a cell phone while driving?
options: They may not use a wireless device at all, even hands-free, except in an emergency
They may use a phone while stopped at a red light
They may use a phone only with a hands-free device
They may make calls but not send texts
questions.explain: All drivers under 18 are barred from using a wireless communication device, including hands-free devices, except in an emergency.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Graduated Driver License (GDL)'

questions.q: A provisional license issued to a 16- or 17-year-old is marked 'PROVISIONAL' and expires:
options: Eight years after it is issued
Two years after it is issued
questions.explain: A provisional license expires on the holder's 18th birthday.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Provisional License'

questions.q: For a first Texas license, an applicant under 18 who is enrolled in school must show attendance of at least how many days in the fall or spring semester before applying?
questions.explain: The Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) form must show at least 80 days of attendance in the preceding fall or spring semester.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) Form'

questions.q: During the school year, the VOE form you bring to the driver license office may not be dated more than how many days before your application?
questions.explain: The VOE may be no more than 30 days old during the school year (90 days during the summer).
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) Form'

questions.q: Which first-time Texas license applicants are required to complete an approved driver education course?
questions.explain: Individuals younger than 25 must successfully complete an approved driver education course; those 18 to 24 take an adult course.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Driver Education'

questions.q: An 18-year-old applying for a first Texas license must complete which driver education course?
questions.explain: Applicants aged 18 through 24 must complete a 6-hour adult driver education course; there is no driver education requirement at 25 and older.
questions.ref: Texas DPS web page 'Choosing a Driver Education Course' (dps.texas.gov, checked October 2026); Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Driver Education'

questions.q: Before the driving exam, every applicant must complete the Impact Texas Drivers (ITD) program. How recent must the ITD certificate be?
options: Dated within one year of the driving test
Any date, as long as it is before the test
Dated within 30 days of the driving test
Dated within 90 days of the driving test
questions.explain: The ITD certificate appropriate to your age must be completed before the driving exam and be dated within 90 days of the driving skills test.
questions.ref: Texas DPS web page 'Apply for a Texas Driver License' (dps.texas.gov, checked October 2026); Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Impact Texas Drivers (ITD)'

questions.q: What score do you need to pass a Texas knowledge (written) exam?
questions.explain: You must score 70 percent or better to pass any Texas knowledge exam.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Part 1: The Knowledge exam'

questions.q: If you do not pass your exams, your application is held for a limited time. When must you submit a new application and pay the fee again?
options: After one year or after five failed exams
After 90 days or after three failed exams
After 30 days or after two failed exams
questions.explain: Texas keeps a failed applicant's file open for 90 days. Once 90 days pass or you fail three exams, you must reapply and pay the fee again.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Examinations'

questions.q: After passing all required exams, you receive a temporary license. How long may you use it?
options: 45 days, or until the permanent card arrives
questions.explain: The temporary license is valid for 45 days or until you receive your permanent license in the mail.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Examinations'

questions.q: Before a teen can get a provisional license, DPS requires how much behind-the-wheel practice?
options: 20 hours, including at least 5 hours at night
30 hours, including at least 10 hours at night
50 hours, including at least 10 hours at night
questions.explain: DPS requires 30 hours of behind-the-wheel practice, at least 10 of them at night, before a teen can apply for a provisional license.
questions.ref: Texas DPS web page 'Texas Provisional License as a Teen' (dps.texas.gov, checked October 2026)

questions.q: How often must a standard Texas driver license be renewed (for drivers 18 to 84)?
questions.explain: A Texas driver license must be renewed every eight years; drivers 85 and older receive two-year licenses.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Application for Renewal'

questions.q: Even if you renew online or by mail, how often must you visit a driver license office in person for a vision check and new photo?
questions.explain: You must appear in person at least once every sixteen years for a vision exam and to update your photo, signature and fingerprints.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Application for Renewal'

questions.q: After you move, how soon must you report your new address to DPS?
questions.explain: A change of address must be reported to DPS within 30 days.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Replacement (Duplicate) or Change of Information on a Driver License or ID Card'

questions.q: What are Texas's minimum liability insurance amounts?
options: $15,000 per injured person, $30,000 per crash for injuries, and $5,000 for property damage
$25,000 per injured person, $50,000 per crash for injuries, and $25,000 for property damage
$30,000 per injured person, $60,000 per crash for injuries, and $25,000 for property damage
$50,000 per injured person, $100,000 per crash for injuries, and $50,000 for property damage
questions.explain: Texas minimums are 30/60/25: $30,000 for one person, $60,000 for two or more people, and $25,000 for property damage.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility, section 'The Liability Insurance Law'

questions.q: What is the fine for a first conviction of driving without proof of financial responsibility (insurance)?
questions.explain: A first conviction carries a fine of $175 to $350; later convictions bring license suspension, a $350–$1,000 fine and possible vehicle impoundment.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility, section 'Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility'

questions.q: What is the maximum fine for a first conviction of driving without a license?
questions.explain: A first conviction for driving without a license is punishable by a fine of up to $200.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Penalties for Driving Without a License'

questions.q: Driving while your license is suspended (with no aggravating factors) is:
options: Only a warning on a first offense
A civil matter with no fine
A felony with mandatory prison time
A Class C misdemeanor with a fine of up to $500
questions.explain: Basic Driving While License Invalid is a Class C misdemeanor punishable by a fine of up to $500; it rises to Class B with a prior conviction, no insurance, or a DWI-related suspension.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Driving While License Invalid (DWLI)'

questions.q: DPS may suspend the license of a driver who is convicted of how many separate traffic violations within any 12-month period?
questions.explain: Repeated violations—four or more convictions in 12 months or seven or more in 24 months—are grounds for suspension after a hearing.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Administrative Suspensions and Revocations'

questions.q: For a driver under 18, DPS may suspend the license after a hearing for how many separate traffic convictions in a 12-month period?
questions.explain: For drivers younger than 18, two or more traffic convictions occurring separately within 12 months are grounds for suspension.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Suspend or Revoke After Hearing of Minor'

questions.q: To whom must you show your driver license when asked?
options: Any person who asks, including other drivers who were not in a crash with you
Only a court clerk after you receive a ticket
A peace officer or judge, and anyone involved in a crash with you
questions.explain: Carry your license when driving and show it on request to any peace officer, sheriff, constable, judge, justice of the peace, or trooper, and to anyone involved in a crash with you.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Pass or Fail Driving Exam'

questions.q: Before a minor's 18th birthday, who can ask DPS to cancel the minor's driver license?
options: Any teacher at the minor's school
The adult who signed the minor's license application
questions.explain: The parent, guardian, or other adult who signed the application may ask in writing, under oath, for the license to be cancelled any time before the minor turns 18.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Minors'

questions.q: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe
Stop only if there is cross traffic
Slow down and go through if no one is coming
Yield to traffic from the left only
questions.explain: A stop sign requires a full stop before the crosswalk, stop line or intersection—slowing down is not enough.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign require you to do?
options: Always come to a full stop
Slow down, and stop if needed to let vehicles, pedestrians or bicyclists on the other road go first
Speed up to merge ahead of other traffic
questions.explain: A yield sign means slow down or stop if necessary to give the right-of-way to traffic on the road you are entering.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Road closed for repairs; detour to the right
You may not enter; traffic on the road ahead flows toward you
questions.explain: This sign marks a one-way road with traffic coming in the opposite direction; entering would put you into oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: If you see this sign facing you, what does it mean?
options: The road ahead curves the wrong way
You are going the wrong way on a one-way road and are facing oncoming traffic
questions.explain: This sign tells you that you are driving against the flow of traffic on a one-way street or ramp.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: This sign is posted on a highway. What does it tell you?
options: The maximum lawful speed; you must go slower if conditions require it
The speed you must drive at all times
The suggested speed for trucks only
questions.explain: A speed limit sign shows the maximum speed permitted; under the basic speed law you may not drive faster than is safe for conditions.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Left turns are not allowed here
questions.explain: Turning left at an intersection where this sign is posted is prohibited.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: U-turns are allowed only on green
You may not make a U-turn here
questions.explain: Making a U-turn where this sign is posted is prohibited.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: You are stopped at a red light and see this sign. What may you do?
options: Turn left after stopping, if it is clear
Turn right after stopping, if it is clear
Wait for a green signal before turning
questions.explain: Right turns on red are normally allowed after a full stop, but not where a sign prohibits turning on red.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Steady Red Light (Stop)'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: Traffic on this street moves only in the direction of the arrow
Passing is allowed in the direction of the arrow
The road ahead is a dead end
Turn in the direction of the arrow immediately
questions.explain: A one-way sign shows that traffic may travel only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you to do?
options: Keep to the right of the island or obstruction ahead
Slower traffic must use the right lane
Turn right at the next intersection
questions.explain: This sign is used ahead of islands and medians: drive to the right of it.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may not pass other vehicles
Do not cross the railroad tracks
questions.explain: This regulatory sign prohibits passing other vehicles.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: You see this sign beside the road. What should you do?
options: Speed up to clear the tracks quickly
Stop every time, even if no train is coming
It marks an abandoned railroad; no action is needed
Slow down, look and listen, and be ready to yield to a train
questions.explain: Crossbuck signs mark the location of tracks at every grade crossing. Slow down, look, listen, and yield to any approaching train.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Railroad Crossbuck'

questions.q: This plaque is mounted below a stop sign. What does it tell you?
options: You may go without stopping if the road is clear
Traffic must stop only during school hours
All approaching traffic must stop; go in order of arrival
questions.explain: It means every approach must stop. Proceed in the order of arrival; if two vehicles arrive together, yield to the one on the right.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: Who may park in a space marked with this sign?
options: Any vehicle with its hazard lights on
A vehicle with a disabled license plate or windshield placard
Anyone parking for less than 15 minutes
questions.explain: Do not park, stop or stand in a disabled-parking space unless the vehicle has a disabled license plate or windshield identification card.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: Turn right at the next street
The lane ends to the right
A side road enters from the right
The road curves gradually in the direction of the arrow; slow down, keep right and do not pass
questions.explain: This warns of a gradual curve ahead in the direction shown. Slow down, keep right, and do not pass.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: A winding road is ahead; drive slowly and do not pass
questions.explain: A winding road is ahead. Drive slowly and carefully, and do not pass.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: The road curves one way and then the other
Passing is allowed after the curve
questions.explain: A reverse curve: the road bends one way and then the other. Slow down, keep right, and do not pass.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A crossroad ahead; watch for traffic from both sides
questions.explain: A cross road is ahead. Slow down and look carefully in all directions for cross traffic.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: The road ends ahead; you must turn left or right and may need to yield
A side road joins from the left
The road continues straight after a short curve
questions.explain: You are approaching a T intersection where you must turn left or right. Be prepared to yield.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: Lanes of traffic are joining your lane from the right
Your lane is ending on the right
questions.explain: Other traffic lanes are coming together with yours ahead. Watch for traffic merging from that direction.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: You are driving in the right lane and see this sign. What should you do?
options: Nothing; the left lane is ending
Speed up to pass traffic on the left
Prepare to merge into the left lane because your lane ends
questions.explain: The lane ends ahead. If you are in the right lane, merge safely into the left lane.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Slow down on a wet road and avoid sudden turns, acceleration or braking
questions.explain: The road is slippery when wet. Slow down and do not suddenly turn, speed up, or stop.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A steep downgrade ahead; you may need a lower gear
A runaway truck ramp is closed
questions.explain: You are approaching a downgrade. Approach with caution; it may be necessary to use a lower gear to control speed.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this five-sided sign?
options: Speed up to clear the area quickly
Stop and wait for a crossing guard
Slow down and watch for children; be ready to stop
questions.explain: This pentagon-shaped sign means you are near a school. Slow down, watch for children, and be prepared to stop suddenly.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this round yellow sign mean?
options: A railroad crossing is a few hundred feet ahead
Railroad tracks are directly under you
questions.explain: The round railroad advance warning sign means you are within a few hundred feet of a crossing. Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Railroad Crossing'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: The distance to the next exit
An underpass with limited height; do not enter if your vehicle or load is taller
questions.explain: The sign shows the height of the underpass. Do not try to pass under if your load is higher than the figure shown.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this pennant-shaped sign mean?
options: You are entering a no-passing zone
questions.explain: The pennant is used only to give advance warning of a no-passing zone.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Traffic Signs (Table: Signs by Shape)'

questions.q: This plaque is shown below a curve warning sign. What does it mean?
options: 35 mph is the highest safe speed for the curve ahead
The speed limit on this road is now 35 mph everywhere
questions.explain: An advisory speed sign gives the highest speed at which you can safely travel around the curve or turn ahead.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: You see this orange sign. What should you expect?
options: A work zone ahead where traffic fines double when workers are present
questions.explain: Orange signs warn of construction and maintenance. Slow down and be ready to stop or change lanes; fines double when workers are present.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Construction and Maintenance Devices'

questions.q: A vehicle displaying this emblem on its rear:
options: Is designed to travel at 25 mph or less
questions.explain: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is required on vehicles designed to operate at a maximum of 25 mph or less, such as farm machinery.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Slow-Moving Vehicle Emblem'

questions.q: This signal is showing a steady light. What does it mean?
options: Stop immediately, even if you are in the intersection
The light is about to turn red; stop before the crosswalk if you can do so safely
Proceed; yellow means the same as green
Speed up to get through before it turns red
questions.explain: A steady yellow warns that red is coming. Stop before the nearest crosswalk if you can do so safely; otherwise proceed cautiously.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Steady Yellow Light (Caution)'

questions.q: What must you do at this signal?
options: Proceed; the light is out of order and has no meaning
Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping
Stop and wait for the light to turn green
Stop completely, then proceed when it is safe
questions.explain: At a flashing red light, stop completely before entering the crosswalk or intersection, then go when safe. Cross traffic may not have to stop.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'A Flashing Red Light'

questions.q: What does this signal mean?
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
The signal is about to turn green
questions.explain: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'A Flashing Yellow Light'

questions.q: What may you do when the signal shows this lit green arrow?
options: Stop and wait until a full green light appears
Turn left carefully after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians still in the intersection
questions.explain: A green arrow (even when shown together with a red light) lets you move carefully in the arrow's direction, but you must first yield to any vehicles and pedestrians still in the intersection.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Green Arrow Displayed at the Same Time as a Red Light'

questions.q: What do these center lines mean?
options: Passing is allowed from either direction when safe
Only drivers on the right side may pass
The lines mark a bicycle lane
Passing is not allowed from either direction
questions.explain: A solid yellow line on your side marks a no-passing zone; with two solid yellow lines, neither direction may pass. On roads of four or more lanes, never cross the double yellow line to pass.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: You are driving the blue car. What do these center lines allow you to do?
options: You may pass when it is safe
questions.explain: A broken line on your side permits passing when safe; the solid line on the other side bars traffic from that direction from passing.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Solid and Broken Lines'

questions.q: What is the center lane marked like this used for?
options: Only for vehicles making a left turn
questions.explain: The center lane is only for vehicles turning left and must not be used for passing or through travel. Enter it only where you have time to slow down for the turn.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Left Turn Lane Only'

questions.q: Which sign shape is used only for stop signs?
questions.explain: The octagon is used exclusively for stop signs.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Traffic Signs (Table: Signs by Shape)'

questions.q: What does an orange sign generally indicate?
options: Motorist services such as food and gas
questions.explain: Orange is the standard color for construction and maintenance warnings.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Traffic Signs (Table: Standard Colors)'

questions.q: An overhead lane-use signal shows a steady red X above your lane. What does it mean?
options: You may drive in that lane
Turn left from that lane only
Prepare to leave the lane soon
Do not drive in that lane
questions.explain: A red X means do not drive in the lane; a steady yellow X means prepare to safely leave the lane; a downward green arrow means the lane is open.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Guide Signs (lane-use control signals)'

questions.q: A flashing yellow left-turn arrow means you may:
options: Not turn left until the arrow is green
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
Turn left; oncoming traffic is stopped
questions.explain: A flashing yellow arrow allows a left turn, but you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'A Flashing Yellow Arrow For Left-Turns'

questions.q: When can you turn left on a steady red light in Texas (unless a sign prohibits it)?
options: When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping
Whenever no traffic is coming, after stopping
Only from a two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explain: On a steady red, after stopping you may turn right, or turn left if both streets are one-way, unless prohibited—yielding to pedestrians and traffic.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Steady Red Light (Stop)'

questions.q: A police officer directing traffic signals you to drive through a red light. You should:
options: Back up and choose another route
Ignore the officer because the signal controls the intersection
Stay stopped until the light turns green
questions.explain: You must obey a law enforcement officer directing traffic at all times, even if told to do something normally against the law, such as going through a red light.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: When is the speed limit on a school zone sign like 'SPEED LIMIT 20 WHEN FLASHING' in effect?
options: When the yellow lights on the sign are flashing
questions.explain: The school zone speed is in effect when the yellow light is flashing. Be extremely careful for children.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: Double solid white lines between lanes mean:
options: They mark a bicycle lane only
You may cross them to pass
questions.explain: Crossing is prohibited where there are double solid white lines; do not change lanes or turn across them.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Solid Lines'

questions.q: You are on a two-lane road arriving at an intersection with a divided highway. There are no signs or signals. Who must yield?
options: Traffic on the divided highway must yield to you
The vehicle on the left goes first
You must yield to traffic on the divided highway
questions.explain: A driver on a single or two-lane road must yield to vehicles on a divided road or a road with three or more lanes.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Single or Two-Lane Road Intersecting a Multi-Lane Road'

questions.q: A driver on an unpaved road reaches an intersection with a paved road. Who has the right-of-way?
options: The driver on the unpaved road
questions.explain: A driver on an unpaved road must yield to vehicles traveling on the paved road.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Unpaved Road Intersecting a Paved Road'

questions.q: At an intersection with no signs, signals, or lane differences, two vehicles approach at about the same time. Which one must yield?
options: The vehicle turning right always yields
The vehicle on the right yields to the vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right
questions.explain: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to any vehicle that has entered or is approaching on your right.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Intersections Not Controlled by Signs, Signals, Multi-Lanes, or Pavement'

questions.q: You are turning left at an intersection and a car is coming straight through from the opposite direction. You must:
options: Turn first because you were there first
questions.explain: When turning left, always yield to vehicles coming straight through from the other direction.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Turning Left'

questions.q: When driving out of a driveway or alley onto a street, you must:
options: Stop only if a pedestrian is on the sidewalk
Stop before the sidewalk and yield to all pedestrians and approaching vehicles
Slow down and merge with traffic without stopping
Sound your horn and pull out, since traffic must yield to you
questions.explain: Coming from a private road, alley, building or driveway, stop before the sidewalk and yield to all approaching vehicles and pedestrians.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Private Roads and Driveways'

questions.q: You are on a street that ends at a T-intersection with a through street. You must:
options: Yield only to vehicles on your right
Stop and yield to traffic on the through street
Proceed first because you are turning
Expect through traffic to stop for you
questions.explain: A driver on a street that ends at a through street must stop and yield to vehicles on the through street.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'T-Intersection'

questions.q: You are driving on the frontage road of a freeway. A car is exiting the freeway onto the frontage road ahead. Who must yield?
options: You, the driver on the frontage road
questions.explain: Frontage road drivers must yield to vehicles entering or about to enter the frontage road from the highway, and to vehicles leaving it to enter the highway.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Enter or Leave Controlled-Access Highway'

questions.q: On a road with three or more lanes going the same way, two cars move into the same middle lane at the same time—one from the right lane and one from the left lane. Who must yield?
options: The car entering from the left lane
The car entering from the right lane
questions.explain: A vehicle entering a lane from the right must yield to a vehicle entering the same lane from the left.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Driving on Multiple-Lane Roads'

questions.q: An ambulance with its siren on is coming up behind you. If traffic allows, you must:
options: Speed up to stay ahead of it
Pull to the right edge of the road and stop
questions.explain: Yield to emergency vehicles using a siren, bell or flashing red light by pulling to the right edge and stopping; if you cannot, slow down and leave a clear path.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Yield Right-of-Way to Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: When following a fire truck that is answering an alarm, you must stay at least how far behind it?
questions.explain: You may not follow within 500 feet of a fire truck answering an alarm or an ambulance with its flashing red lights on.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Yield Right-of-Way to Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: On a road posted at 65 mph with only one lane in your direction, you approach a police car stopped on the shoulder with its lights flashing. You must slow to no more than:
questions.explain: If you cannot vacate the lane, slow to at least 20 mph below the posted limit when the limit is 25 mph or more: 65 − 20 = 45 mph.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Yield Right-of-Way to Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: On a street posted at 20 mph, you pass a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights on. You must slow to:
options: No change is needed below 25 mph
questions.explain: When the posted limit is below 25 mph, the move-over/slow-down law requires slowing to less than 5 mph.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Yield Right-of-Way to Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: On a highway with two lanes in your direction, you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with lights activated in the right lane's shoulder. Unless an officer directs otherwise, you should:
options: Stop completely behind the emergency vehicle
Stay in your lane and keep your speed
Drive onto the shoulder to give room
Move out of the lane closest to the emergency vehicle
questions.explain: On roads with two or more lanes in that direction, vacate the lane closest to the stopped emergency vehicle (or slow to 20 mph below the limit).
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Yield Right-of-Way to Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: Texas's 'Slow Down or Move Over' law applies when which vehicle is stopped on the road with its lights on?
options: A city bus at a bus stop
A car with a flat tire and no lights
questions.explain: The law covers emergency medical vehicles, police, fire trucks, tow trucks, utility service vehicles and TxDOT or other highway maintenance vehicles with lights activated.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Slow Down or Move Over'

questions.q: On a two-lane road, a school bus coming toward you stops and turns on its alternately flashing red lights. You must:
options: Slow to 20 mph and pass carefully
Continue, because you are going the opposite way
Stop only if children are visible
questions.explain: You must stop when approaching a school bus from either direction that is displaying alternately flashing red lights.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Yield Right-of-Way to School Buses'

questions.q: After stopping for a school bus with flashing red lights, when may you go?
options: When the bus starts moving, the driver signals you to go, or the red lights stop flashing
As soon as no children are in the road
After the stop arm begins to fold, even if the lights are still flashing
questions.explain: Do not pass until the bus resumes motion, the driver signals you to proceed, or the red lights are no longer flashing.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Yield Right-of-Way to School Buses'

questions.q: In which situation are you NOT required to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?
options: The bus is on a different road from the one you are on
The bus is on the other side of a two-lane road
You are behind the bus on a four-lane undivided street
questions.explain: Stopping is not required when the bus is on a different road, or on a controlled-access highway where the bus is in a loading zone and pedestrians may not cross.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Yield Right-of-Way to School Buses'

questions.q: What is the fine for a first conviction of illegally passing a stopped school bus?
questions.explain: A first conviction carries a fine of $500 to $1,250; a second within five years brings $1,000 to $2,000 and a possible six-month suspension.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Yield Right-of-Way to School Buses'

questions.q: Your light turns green, but a pedestrian who started crossing earlier is still in the crosswalk. You must:
options: Proceed, because you have a green light
Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing
questions.explain: If the light changes after a pedestrian has entered the crosswalk, you must still give the pedestrian the right-of-way.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Yield the Right-of-Way to Pedestrians (Persons on Foot)'

questions.q: At an intersection with a green light but no pedestrian signal, a pedestrian is crossing in front of you. Who has the right-of-way?
options: You, because you have the green light
The pedestrian only if using a cane
questions.explain: If there is no pedestrian control signal, give pedestrians the right-of-way on a green light.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Yield the Right-of-Way to Pedestrians (Persons on Foot)'

questions.q: Which statement about right-of-way is correct?
options: If you have the right-of-way, you may proceed no matter what
Right-of-way is given, not taken; yield if another driver does not
Right-of-way rules apply only at signals
The faster vehicle always has the right-of-way
questions.explain: Right-of-way is something given, not taken. If another driver does not follow the rules, let them go.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Chapter 4 introduction'

questions.q: When you must stop for a train at a railroad crossing, how far from the nearest rail must you stop?
questions.explain: Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail when a signal, gate, flagger, or approaching train requires it.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Railroad Grade Crossings'

questions.q: A train within about 1,500 feet of a crossing sounds its horn. What must you do?
options: Stop and stay stopped until it is safe to cross
Stop only if the lights are flashing
Cross quickly before the train arrives
Slow down and cross if the gates are still up
questions.explain: You must stop when an approaching train is within about 1,500 feet and gives an audible signal, and remain stopped until it is safe.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Railroad Grade Crossings'

questions.q: What is the fine range for disobeying the law at a railroad grade crossing?
questions.explain: A person who fails to obey railroad grade crossing laws faces a fine of $50 to $200.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Railroad Grade Crossings'

questions.q: When entering a freeway from an on-ramp, you must:
options: Expect freeway traffic to make room for you
Stop at the end of the ramp
Yield to vehicles already on the freeway
Enter at a slow speed and let others go around
questions.explain: Yield the right-of-way to vehicles already on the highway, then use the speed change lane to match traffic speed and merge.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Entering the Highway'

questions.q: At an all-way stop, you and another vehicle stop at the same time. The other vehicle is on your right. What should you do?
options: Go first because it is on your right
Let the vehicle on your right go first
Go first if you are going straight
Wait for a third vehicle to decide
questions.explain: Every driver stops and goes in the order they arrived; when two arrive together, the driver on the left lets the driver on the right go first.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: When entering a modern roundabout, you must:
options: Yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout
Expect circulating traffic to yield to you
Stop even if the circle is empty
Enter to the left and travel clockwise
questions.explain: Slow down, yield to traffic already in the circle, enter when there is a gap, and travel counterclockwise.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: A driver who fails to yield the right-of-way and causes bodily injury to another person faces a fine of:
questions.explain: Failure to yield causing bodily injury is punishable by a fine of $500 to $2,000 ($1,000 to $4,000 for serious bodily injury).
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Right-of-Way (Table: Penalties for Failure to Yield Right-of-Way)'

questions.q: A pedestrian carrying a white cane is crossing the street ahead of you. What does the law require?
options: Yield only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk
Sound your horn to warn the pedestrian
Proceed if you have a green light
Take all needed precautions, and come to a full stop if that is the only way to avoid danger
questions.explain: A white cane indicates the person may be blind or disabled. Drivers must take necessary precautions and stop if needed to avoid injuring them.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety, section 'Laws and Safety Tips for Motorists'

questions.q: A pedestrian crosses the street in the middle of the block, away from any crosswalk. Under Texas law, the pedestrian:
options: May cross only if carrying a light
Must yield the right-of-way to vehicles
Has the right-of-way only at night
questions.explain: A pedestrian crossing anywhere other than within a crosswalk at an intersection must yield to vehicles (drivers must still try to avoid hitting them).
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety, section 'Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians'

questions.q: Who has the right-of-way at a railroad crossing?
options: Vehicles, if the crossing has no gates
The first vehicle to reach the crossing
questions.explain: A train cannot stop quickly and does not stop for crossings, so it always has the right-of-way.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Additional Safe Driving Procedures at Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: Unless another limit is posted, what is the speed limit in a Texas urban district?
questions.explain: The prima facie speed limit in an urban district is 30 mph.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in an alley?
questions.explain: The speed limit in an alley is 15 mph.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed for a passenger car on a U.S. or Texas-numbered highway (including Farm-to-Market roads) outside an urban district?
questions.explain: Numbered highways outside urban districts have a 70 mph limit for passenger cars unless another limit is posted.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed for a passenger car on a highway outside an urban district that is NOT numbered by Texas or the U.S.?
questions.explain: On un-numbered highways outside an urban district, the limit is 60 mph.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: On a public beach where the county commissioners court has set a limit, the speed limit is:
questions.explain: Beaches and county roads next to a public beach (if declared by the commissioners court) have a 15 mph limit.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: Some Texas limited-access highways have posted speed limits as high as:
questions.explain: Based on traffic studies, many limited-access highways are posted at 75 up to 85 mph. Always obey the posted limit.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: When a city or county sets or changes a speed limit, what must be true about daytime and nighttime limits?
options: The nighttime limit must be 5 mph lower
The nighttime limit must be 10 mph lower
Only a daytime limit is set
questions.explain: Entities that establish or alter a speed limit must set the same limit for daytime and nighttime.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: In good conditions at 30 mph or less, what is the minimum following time behind the car ahead?
questions.explain: At speeds of 30 mph or less in good road conditions, keep at least 2 seconds between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed'

questions.q: In good conditions at speeds above 30 mph, the Texas handbook says to keep a following gap of:
questions.explain: Above 30 mph, maintain a 4-second gap in good conditions, and more in poor conditions. Four seconds is also the best practice for new drivers.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed'

questions.q: How do you check your following distance?
options: Count the seconds from when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed object until you reach it
Keep the car ahead's bumper visible over your hood
Watch your speedometer and stay 10 mph slower
Count the car lengths between you and the vehicle ahead
questions.explain: Pick a fixed object; when the vehicle ahead passes it, count until you reach it. Reaching it in under two seconds means you are too close.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed'

questions.q: With good brakes on dry, level pavement, about how many feet does it take an average driver to stop from 70 mph (including reaction distance)?
questions.explain: The handbook's stopping table shows about 387 feet to stop from 70 mph, even with good brakes and tires on dry, level pavement.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Approximate Stopping Distances'

questions.q: About how many feet does it take to stop from 50 mph (thinking plus braking distance) on dry pavement?
questions.explain: The stopping table gives about 229 feet at 50 mph.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Approximate Stopping Distances'

questions.q: About how many feet does it take to stop from 20 mph on dry pavement?
questions.explain: At 20 mph the total stopping distance is about 63 feet.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Approximate Stopping Distances'

questions.q: About how long does it take the average driver to think, react and apply the brakes?
questions.explain: It takes the average person about 1½ seconds to think, react and apply the brakes.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Approximate Stopping Distances'

questions.q: How does higher speed affect your field of vision?
options: It narrows it—at 60 mph you see only about one-fifth of what you see when stopped
It widens it because you scan more
questions.explain: Speed reduces your field of vision: about 2/3 at 20 mph, 2/5 at 40 mph, and 1/5 at 60 mph.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed Reduces Your Field of Vision'

questions.q: The posted limit is 55 mph, but there is heavy rain and poor visibility. What speed is legal?
options: Any speed, as long as your headlights are on
Up to 60 mph to keep up with traffic
A speed slower than 55 that is safe for the conditions
questions.explain: Under the basic speed law you may not drive faster than is safe and prudent for conditions, regardless of the posted limit.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed Limits'; Appendix A: Glossary, 'basic speed law'

questions.q: What should you do when the road is wet or crowded, or when your vision is limited?
options: Slow down and increase your following distance
Keep the same speed but use high beams
Speed up to get through quickly
Follow closer so you can see the taillights ahead
questions.explain: Slow down and increase following distance on wet or crowded roads and when your vision is limited.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed'

questions.q: In a construction or maintenance work zone, traffic fines:
options: Are the same as anywhere else
questions.explain: Fines double in a construction or maintenance work zone when workers are present.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Obey Warning Signs and Barricades'

questions.q: If you cannot or do not want to drive at least the minimum posted speed on a highway, you should:
options: Drive at any speed you choose in the right lane
Turn on your hazard lights and drive in the left lane
questions.explain: Drivers who are unable or unwilling to keep up with the posted minimum speed should stay off that highway.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Before Using a Highway'

questions.q: Taking part in a street race or drag race on a public road in Texas is:
options: A crime ranging from a Class B misdemeanor to a second-degree felony
Legal at night when roads are empty
questions.explain: Street racing is illegal; penalties range from a Class B misdemeanor up to a second-degree felony.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Street Racing'

questions.q: When should you begin slowing down when leaving a freeway?
options: You should not slow down until you see a stop sign
On the freeway, well before the exit ramp
Only after you reach the end of the ramp
On the exit ramp, so you are within the new, lower speed by the end of the ramp
questions.explain: Do your slowing on the exit ramp itself, so you are down to the lower posted speed by the time you leave the ramp.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Leaving the Highway'

questions.q: At night, how fast should you drive?
options: Slowly enough to stop within the distance lit by your headlights
As fast as the vehicle ahead
At the posted limit, regardless of visibility
Faster than in the day because traffic is lighter
questions.explain: Slow down at night and make sure you can stop within the distance your headlights light up.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Headlights'

questions.q: On a freeway, you should generally:
options: Change lanes often to find the fastest lane
Drive in the left lane at the minimum speed
Speed up and slow down to keep others from passing
Keep pace with traffic, maintain a steady speed and avoid weaving
questions.explain: Stay in the middle of your lane, don't weave, and keep a constant speed with the flow of traffic.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Once You are in the Proper Lane'

questions.q: How far before turning must you signal continuously?
questions.explain: Signal continuously for at least 100 feet before turning or stopping, and turn the signal off after the turn.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'How to Signal'

questions.q: To signal a left turn by hand, you extend your left arm:
options: Out and wave it back and forth
questions.explain: Left turn: left arm straight out. Right turn: arm bent upward. Stop or slow: arm bent downward.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'How to Signal'

questions.q: A driver's left arm is extended out the window and bent upward at the elbow. This driver intends to:
options: Pull over for an emergency vehicle
questions.explain: A left arm bent upward is the hand signal for a right turn.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'How to Signal'

questions.q: A driver's left arm is extended out the window and pointed downward. This driver intends to:
questions.explain: A left arm bent downward means the driver is stopping or slowing down.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'How to Signal'

questions.q: Which of these requires a turn signal?
options: Slowing for a speed bump in a parking lot with no one around
Pulling away from a parallel parking space at the curb
questions.explain: Signal to change lanes, turn, pull away from a parallel parking space, slow or stop, enter or leave a highway, and pull to the side of the road.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'Signaling'

questions.q: You may not drive on the left side of the road within how many feet of an intersection or railroad crossing?
questions.explain: Never drive on the left side within 100 feet of or while crossing an intersection or railroad crossing.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'Keep to the Right'

questions.q: You may not drive on the left side of the road to pass within how many feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel?
questions.explain: Passing on the left is prohibited within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'Keep to the Right'

questions.q: In which situation is it illegal to drive on the left side of the road to pass?
options: On a hill or curve where your view is limited
On a straight two-lane road with a broken yellow line and no oncoming traffic
When the right half of the road is closed
questions.explain: Never drive on the left on a hill, curve, or other place with limited vision, in a no-passing zone, or on roads with two or more lanes in each direction.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'Keep to the Right'

questions.q: When passing on a two-lane road, you must be able to return to the right lane before an oncoming vehicle comes within:
questions.explain: Be sure you have time and space to pass and return to the right lane before an approaching car comes within 200 feet.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'How to Pass on a Two-Lane Road'

questions.q: After passing a car, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: When the other driver flashes the high beams, regardless of distance
As soon as your front bumper is past its front bumper
When you can see the passed car in your rearview mirror
questions.explain: Do not return until you have safely cleared the vehicle—wait until you can see it in your rearview mirror.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'How to Pass on a Two-Lane Road'

questions.q: When may you pass another vehicle on the right in Texas?
options: On a road with two or more lanes in each direction that is clear of obstructions, or on a one-way road
By driving onto an unpaved shoulder
Whenever the driver ahead is going below the limit
questions.explain: Passing on the right is allowed only when safe: on roads wide enough for two or more lanes each way and clear of obstructions, on one-way roads, or on a paved shoulder in limited cases.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'Passing on the Right'

questions.q: You may use a paved shoulder to pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is:
options: Stopped or preparing to turn left
questions.explain: Passing on a paved shoulder is allowed when the vehicle ahead is slowing or stopped on the main road, disabled, or preparing to turn left. Never pass off the paved portion of the road.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'Passing on the Right'

questions.q: Another vehicle is passing you on the left. You should:
options: Speed up so the pass is shorter
Stay in your lane and not speed up
Move to the left to block the pass
questions.explain: When being passed, do not increase your speed, stay in your lane, and make it as easy as possible for the other driver.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'When Another Vehicle is Passing'

questions.q: You are near an intersection and realize you are not in the correct lane to turn, and you cannot safely get there within half a block. You should:
options: Stop in your lane until you can move over
Turn from the lane you are in
Back up to the correct lane
Continue straight and find another way back
questions.explain: If you cannot move into the proper lane at least half a block before the turn, skip the turn and keep going straight.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'Turning'

questions.q: When making a right turn, you should:
options: Swing wide to the left first
Signal, slow down, and keep as close as possible to the right edge of the road
questions.explain: Move to the far right lane, signal and slow at least 100 feet from the corner, and keep as close as possible to the right edge.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'How to Make a Right Turn'

questions.q: When making a left turn from a two-way street onto another two-way street, where should you finish your turn?
options: In any lane, as long as you signal
To the right of the center line of the street you enter
In the far left lane of the new street, against traffic
questions.explain: Stay to the right of the center line as you enter, and complete the turn to the right of the center line of the road you are turning into.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'How to Make a Left Turn'

questions.q: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should enter:
options: The lane in which you will interfere least with other traffic
The lane closest to the oncoming traffic
questions.explain: When turning left onto a one-way street, enter the lane where you will interfere the least with other traffic.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'Making a Left Turn From a Two-Way Onto a One-Way Street'

questions.q: How should you use a center left-turn lane?
options: Use it to pass slow traffic
Use it to merge into traffic from a side street at high speed
Enter it only where you have time to slow or stop for your left turn
Drive in it for several blocks to bypass congestion
questions.explain: The center lane is only for vehicles turning left; never use it for passing or through traffic.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Left Turn Lane Only'

questions.q: On a road with several lanes in your direction, the farthest left lane is meant for:
questions.explain: Slower traffic should use a lane other than the farthest left lane, which is for passing only.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Regulatory and Warning Signs'

questions.q: When passing another vehicle, you should avoid:
options: Lingering in the other driver's blind spot
questions.explain: Do not drive or linger in another driver's blind spot; either pass or drop back.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'Blind Spot Driving'

questions.q: When you plan to exit a busy freeway, you should:
options: Move into the exit lane well before the exit
Cross several lanes right at the exit
Slow down in the travel lane before moving over
Stay in the left lane until the last moment
questions.explain: Move into the proper lane well before the exit—the heavier the traffic, the earlier. Exit signs are usually at least 1,000 yards ahead.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Leaving the Highway'

questions.q: How should you enter a freeway?
options: Drive onto the shoulder until a gap appears
Use the acceleration lane, signal, and speed up to merge with the flow when clear
Merge at a low speed and let traffic go around you
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap
questions.explain: Enter the speed change lane, stay right, signal left, and increase speed to merge with the flow of traffic when it is clear.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Entering the Highway'

questions.q: On a multi-lane freeway, which lane should you use if you are driving slower than other traffic?
questions.explain: Use the right lane at the minimum speed or below the normal flow; use middle or left lanes to travel faster or pass.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Choose the Proper Lane'

questions.q: Inside a modern roundabout, traffic travels:
options: Clockwise, and you exit by turning left
Counterclockwise, and you exit by turning right
questions.explain: A modern roundabout is a one-way circle; traffic flows counterclockwise and you signal right to exit.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: In a multi-lane roundabout, you should:
options: Stop in the circle to let others merge
Change lanes freely inside the circle
Pick the correct lane before entering and not change lanes in the circle
questions.explain: Use the lane-movement sign to choose your entry lane, and do not change lanes while in the circle.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: On a highway with four or more lanes and a double yellow center line, you may:
options: Never cross the double yellow line to pass
Cross it to pass when the road is clear
questions.explain: On multi-lane highways, do not cross the double yellow line to pass. Stay in your lane and keep right if driving slower.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Multi-lane Highway (Four or More Lanes)'

questions.q: What should you do after completing a turn or lane change?
options: Make sure your turn signal is off
Leave the signal on for the next turn
questions.explain: Turn off your signal once the turn is complete—an unintended signal still tells others you plan to turn.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning, section 'How to Signal'

questions.q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park?
questions.explain: Do not park or stand within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Do Not Park or Stand a Vehicle'

questions.q: When parking near a corner, how far must you stay from a crosswalk at an intersection?
questions.explain: Do not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Do Not Park or Stand a Vehicle'

questions.q: How far must you park from a stop sign, yield sign, or flashing signal on the approach side?
questions.explain: Do not park within 30 feet on the approach to a flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal at the side of the road.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Do Not Park or Stand a Vehicle'

questions.q: On the same side of the street as a fire station's driveway, you may not park within:
questions.explain: Do not park within 20 feet of a fire station driveway on the same side; on the opposite side, stay 75 feet from the entrance.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Do Not Park or Stand a Vehicle'

questions.q: On the side of the street opposite a fire station entrance, how far away must you park?
questions.explain: On the side opposite a fire station entrance, do not park within 75 feet of the entrance.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Do Not Park or Stand a Vehicle'

questions.q: How close may you park to the nearest rail of a railroad crossing?
questions.explain: Do not park within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Do Not Park a Vehicle'

questions.q: When parallel parked, your curb-side wheels may be no more than how far from the curb?
questions.explain: Your curb-side wheels may be at most 18 inches from the curb or road edge; about 6 inches is ideal.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Parallel Parking'

questions.q: When starting to parallel park, how far out from the parked car ahead of the space should you stop?
questions.explain: Signal, then stop even with the front car about two feet out from it before backing into the space.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Parallel Parking'

questions.q: You park uphill next to a curb. How should you turn your front wheels?
options: It does not matter if the parking brake is set
Away from the curb, so the back of the front tire rests against it
questions.explain: Uphill with a curb: turn the wheels away from the curb so the back of the wheel rests against it; if the car rolls, the curb stops it.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Parking on Hills'

questions.q: You park downhill next to a curb. How should you turn your front wheels?
options: Toward the center of the street
questions.explain: When parking downhill with a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Parking on Hills'

questions.q: You park on a hill on a road with no curb. Which way should your front wheels point?
options: Left when uphill and straight when downhill
Toward the center of the road (to the left)
Toward the edge of the road (to the right)
questions.explain: With no curb, turn the wheels to the right, toward the edge of the road, so the car would roll away from traffic.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Parking on Hills'

questions.q: In which of these places is stopping, standing, or parking prohibited (except to avoid conflict with traffic or obey an officer or signal)?
questions.explain: You may not park, stop or stand on a bridge, elevated structure, or in a highway tunnel, nor in an intersection, on a crosswalk or sidewalk, or on railroad tracks.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Do Not Park, Stop, or Stand a Vehicle'

questions.q: Stopping or parking on the roadway side of a vehicle already parked at the curb ('double parking') is:
options: Allowed if your hazard lights are on
Allowed for up to five minutes
Allowed for deliveries at any time
questions.explain: Stopping, standing or parking beside a vehicle that is already stopped or parked at the curb (double parking) is prohibited.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Do Not Park, Stop, or Stand a Vehicle'

questions.q: Before leaving your vehicle unattended, Texas law requires you to:
options: Leave the engine running if you will be back within five minutes
Stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key and set the brake
questions.explain: It is illegal to leave a vehicle unattended without turning off the engine, locking the ignition, removing the key, and setting the brake (and turning the wheels to the curb on a grade).
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Unattended Motor Vehicle'

questions.q: What is the fine for a first offense of illegally parking in a space reserved for people with disabilities?
questions.explain: Illegally parking in a disabled space is a misdemeanor with a fine of $500 to $750 for a first offense, rising to $1,250 for five or more offenses.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Disabled Parking'

questions.q: May you park in the striped area next to a disabled parking space?
options: No; those areas are for wheelchair lifts and access
