Yes, if you have a compact car
Yes, if all other spaces are full
questions.explain: Do not park in striped areas next to disabled parking spaces; they are needed for wheelchair lifts.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Disabled Parking'

questions.q: When may you use someone else's disabled-parking windshield placard?
options: When you are running an errand for them
Any time you borrow their car
Only when you are transporting the person to whom it was issued
questions.explain: A disabled-parking placard may be used only when transporting the disabled person to whom it was issued; it may not be lent.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Disabled Parking'

questions.q: Outside a business or residential district, if you must stop on the paved part of a highway, your vehicle must be visible from each direction for at least:
questions.explain: If you cannot park off the road, leave room for others to pass and be sure your vehicle can be seen for at least 200 feet in each direction.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Parking, Stopping, or Standing on a Highway Outside an Urban Area'

questions.q: If you must park on an unlighted highway at night, you should:
options: Leave your parking lights or low-beam headlights on
Turn on only the interior light
Turn all lights off to save the battery
questions.explain: At night, use your parking lights or leave your headlights on low beam when parked on an unlit highway.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Headlights'; Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Parking, Stopping, or Standing on a Highway Outside an Urban Area'

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a legal place to park or stand?
options: Thirty feet from a fire hydrant
In a marked space in a parking lot
In front of a public or private driveway
questions.explain: Whether occupied or not, you may not park or stand in front of a public or private driveway.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Do Not Park or Stand a Vehicle'

questions.q: Compared with passing a car, passing a large truck on a level highway takes about:
questions.explain: On level ground, passing a truck takes roughly 3 to 5 seconds more than passing a car.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Share the Road with Trucks (Passing)'

questions.q: After passing a large truck, when is it safe to move back in front of it?
options: Immediately, so you don't stay alongside
When the whole front of the truck is visible in your rearview mirror
As soon as you are past its cab
When you are one car length ahead
questions.explain: Wait until the whole front of the truck appears in your rearview mirror before moving back in, then keep your speed up.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Share the Road with Trucks (Passing)'

questions.q: When you are following a tractor-trailer, a good rule of thumb is:
options: If you can't see the driver in the truck's side mirror, the driver can't see you
Flash your high beams so the driver sees you
Stay directly behind the trailer so the driver knows where you are
Follow closely to stay out of the wind
questions.explain: Stay out of the truck's rear blind spot; if you cannot see the driver in the side mirror, the driver cannot see you.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Following a Truck'

questions.q: When following a truck at night, you should:
options: Use your high beams so the driver sees you
questions.explain: Always dim your headlights when following a truck at night; bright lights reflect off its large mirrors and blind the driver.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Following a Truck'

questions.q: You are stopped behind a truck on an uphill grade. You should:
options: Leave extra space in case it rolls back, and stay to the left in your lane
Stay to the right in your lane
Sound your horn so it knows you are there
questions.explain: Leave space in case the truck drifts back as it starts, and keep to the left in your lane so the driver can see you.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Following a Truck'

questions.q: A large truck ahead is signaling a right turn and has moved left, leaving space on its right. You should:
options: Honk and pass on the left
Stay behind the truck and not pass on the right
Quickly pass on the right before it turns
questions.explain: Trucks make wide right turns and may leave an open space on the right. Don't pass on the right if the truck might turn.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Right Turns'

questions.q: A truck is backing into a loading area and is blocking the road. You should:
options: Wait until it finishes the maneuver
questions.explain: Never cross behind a truck preparing to back up; wait for it to complete its maneuver.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Backing Crashes'

questions.q: A loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph may need how much distance to stop?
options: About 240 feet, the same as a car
questions.explain: A car at 55 mph can stop in about 240 feet; a fully loaded tractor-trailer may need more than 400 feet.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Following a Truck'

questions.q: When you meet a large truck coming from the opposite direction, you should:
options: Keep as far to the side of your lane as possible
questions.explain: Keep as far to the side as possible to avoid a sideswipe and reduce wind turbulence, which pushes vehicles apart.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Share the Road with Trucks (Passing)'

questions.q: How much of a lane is a motorcycle entitled to?
options: Only the right third of the lane
None; motorcycles must ride on the shoulder
questions.explain: Allow a motorcyclist a full lane width; do not try to share the lane with a motorcycle.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Respect a Motorcycle'

questions.q: When following a motorcycle, allow at least:
options: 2 seconds, the same as for a car
questions.explain: Allow more following distance—at least four to six seconds—behind a motorcycle.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Allow Plenty of Space When Following a Motorcycle'

questions.q: What is the most common crash between a car and a motorcycle?
options: A car turning left in front of a motorcycle at an intersection
A car backing out of a driveway
A motorcycle running off the road on a curve
A motorcycle rear-ending a car on the freeway
questions.explain: The most common car–motorcycle crash happens when a car makes a left turn in front of a motorcycle at an intersection.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Left Turns'

questions.q: A motorcycle approaching you has its turn signal flashing. You should:
options: Pull out, since the motorcycle is turning
Flash your lights at the rider
Speed up to get ahead of it
Wait to be sure it is actually turning before you proceed
questions.explain: Motorcycle signals usually are not self-canceling and riders sometimes forget them; make sure the rider is turning before you go.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Signal Your Intentions'

questions.q: Under Texas law, a person riding a bicycle on the road:
options: Has the same rights and responsibilities as a driver of a vehicle
Has no right to use a traffic lane
Must always ride on the sidewalk
questions.explain: A bicycle is a vehicle, and its rider has the same rights and duties as other drivers.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Share the Road with Bicycles'

questions.q: A bicyclist may use the full lane, instead of riding near the right edge, when the outside lane is narrower than:
questions.explain: A bicyclist may take the lane when it is less than 14 feet wide without an adjacent bike lane, or otherwise too narrow to share safely.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety, section 'Bicycle Traffic Laws'

questions.q: You are about to turn right and a bicyclist is riding beside you on the right. You should:
options: Turn quickly in front of the bicycle
Slow down and merge behind the bicycle, then turn
Honk to make the cyclist stop
Turn from the left lane to avoid the cyclist
questions.explain: A motorist should slow and merge with bicycle traffic before a right turn instead of turning across the cyclist's path.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Car-Bicycle Crashes'

questions.q: A bicycle ridden at night in Texas must have a white front lamp visible from at least:
questions.explain: At night a bicycle needs a front white lamp visible from at least 500 feet and a red rear reflector (a red rear light may be added).
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety, section 'Bicycles Must Be Properly Equipped'

questions.q: A bicyclist extends the right arm straight out horizontally. The rider intends to:
questions.explain: Bicyclists signal a right turn with the left arm pointed up or the right arm extended horizontally.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety, section 'Bicycle Traffic Laws'

questions.q: You see a small flag on the back of a bicycle. What might it indicate?
options: The rider may be hearing impaired
The rider is in a race
questions.explain: A safety flag on a bicycle (or a vehicle) may show that the operator is hearing impaired; slow down.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Hearing Impaired'

questions.q: Why must drivers be especially careful near light rail trains?
options: They must yield to cars at crossings
They only run in one direction
They are very quiet and cannot stop quickly
questions.explain: Light rail is quieter than most cars and buses, travels in both directions, and cannot start or stop quickly. Never drive around crossing gates.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Share the Road with Light Rail'

questions.q: Ahead of you, a mail truck is making frequent stops in your lane. You should:
options: Follow closely so you can pass quickly
Proceed with caution and change lanes if possible before passing
Sound your horn to make it move
questions.explain: Mail, delivery, and trash vehicles stop frequently in the road. Proceed with caution and, if possible, change lanes before passing.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Slow Down or Move Over'

questions.q: Where there are no sidewalks, pedestrians should walk:
options: On the left side of the road, facing traffic
On the right side, with traffic
In the middle of the lane
questions.explain: Pedestrians should walk on the left side when there are no sidewalks and step off the pavement when a car approaches.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety, section 'Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians'

questions.q: A neighborhood electric vehicle may be driven only on streets with a posted speed limit of:
questions.explain: Neighborhood electric vehicles may be used on streets posted at 45 mph or less; motor-assisted scooters on streets posted at 35 mph or less.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters'

questions.q: Why do many drivers misjudge an approaching tractor-trailer at an intersection?
options: Its lights are dimmer than a car's
It must stop at every intersection
It always travels below the speed limit
Its large size makes it seem slower than it really is
questions.explain: Because of its size, a tractor-trailer often appears to be moving slower than it is, a factor in many intersection crashes.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Never Underestimate the Size and Speed of an Approaching Tractor-trailer'

questions.q: When are you required to use headlights in Texas?
options: Only after dark when streetlights are off
From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and whenever you cannot see clearly for 1,000 feet
questions.explain: Headlights are required from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and any time people or vehicles cannot be seen clearly at 1,000 feet.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Headlights'

questions.q: You must switch to low beams when an oncoming vehicle is within:
questions.explain: Use low beams within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Headlights'

questions.q: You must use low beams when following another vehicle within:
questions.explain: Dim your lights when following closely, within 300 feet, behind another vehicle.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Headlights'

questions.q: Which headlights should you use in fog, heavy rain, sleet, snow, or dust?
questions.explain: Use low-beam headlights in fog, heavy rain, sleet, snow, or dust; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Headlights'

questions.q: To avoid being blinded by the headlights of an oncoming car at night, you should:
options: Look toward the lower right side of your lane
questions.explain: Avoid looking into oncoming headlights; shift your eyes down to the lower right side of your lane.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Headlights'

questions.q: To fight highway hypnosis on a long trip, the handbook recommends stopping at least every:
questions.explain: Stop at least every two hours or every 100 miles, get out and walk around, and don't drive more than eight hours a day.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Fight Highway Hypnosis'

questions.q: Under Texas law, a driver of any age may not:
options: Use a navigation system mounted on the dashboard
Read, write, or send an electronic message on a phone while driving
questions.explain: Texas law bars every driver from reading, writing or sending electronic messages on a phone or other portable wireless device while driving.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Texting While Driving'

questions.q: Who must wear a seat belt in a passenger vehicle in Texas?
options: Only the driver and front-seat passenger
The driver and every passenger, in every seat that has a belt
questions.explain: The driver and all passengers, regardless of age or seat, must use safety belts if the seat is equipped with one.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'Safety Belts'

questions.q: A child must ride in a federally approved child safety seat if the child is:
options: Younger than 8, unless taller than 4 feet 9 inches
questions.explain: Any child under 8 years old must be in a child safety seat unless the child is more than 4'9" tall.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'Safety Belts'

questions.q: If a passenger under 17 is not wearing a seat belt, who gets the fine?
options: No one; it is a warning only
questions.explain: The driver is fined $100 to $200 for each passenger under 17 riding without a safety belt.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'Penalties for Driving Without a Safety Belt'

questions.q: What is the fine range for a driver who is not wearing a seat belt?
questions.explain: Driving without a safety belt carries a fine of $25 to $50.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'Penalties for Driving Without a Safety Belt'

questions.q: Texas law generally prohibits a child under what age from riding in the open bed of a pickup?
questions.explain: It is an offense to drive an open-bed or flatbed truck with a child younger than 18 in the bed, except in limited situations such as parades or emergencies.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'Vehicles with Open Beds'

questions.q: Your car begins to skid. What should you do first?
options: Take your foot off the gas and steer in the direction of the skid
Steer hard in the opposite direction
Shift into neutral and pull the parking brake
questions.explain: Don't brake suddenly; ease off the accelerator and turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid, then straighten as you regain control.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Steering Out of a Skid'

questions.q: If your brakes fail, you should:
options: Shift to a lower gear and apply the parking brake carefully
Pull the parking brake as hard as possible
questions.explain: Don't panic: use the parking brake cautiously so you don't lock the wheels, and shift to a lower gear.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Brake Failure'

questions.q: Your right wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder. You should:
options: Ease off the gas, brake gently, and return to the pavement when your speed is reduced and traffic is clear
Brake hard and steer sharply back onto the road
Stop immediately on the shoulder edge
questions.explain: Don't brake hard or swing back. Grip the wheel, take your foot off the gas, slow down, check traffic, and carefully drive back onto the pavement.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Running Off the Pavement'

questions.q: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:
options: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, brake gently and steer straight to a stop
questions.explain: With a blowout, don't brake hard; take your foot off the gas, apply the brakes gently, and steer straight ahead to a stop.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Flat Tire or Blowout'

questions.q: When driving down a long, steep hill, you should:
options: Ride the brakes the whole way
Shift into a lower gear to help control your speed
questions.explain: Shift into a low gear to help slow the vehicle. Never coast in neutral (or with the clutch pressed in).
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Driving Down a Steep Hill'

questions.q: Coasting downhill with the transmission in neutral is:
questions.explain: Texas law forbids coasting downhill with the vehicle in neutral.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 7: Parking, Stopping, or Standing, section 'Coasting'

questions.q: In winter, where is ice most likely to form first?
options: On bridges and in shaded areas
questions.explain: Bridges may be icy when the rest of the pavement is clear, and snow melts more slowly in shady areas.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Winter Driving'

questions.q: About how deep must water be to float many cars?
questions.explain: Six inches of water reaches the bottom of most cars, 12 inches will float many cars, and two feet of rushing water can carry away most vehicles.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Floods'

questions.q: About how much water will reach the bottom of most passenger cars and can cause loss of control or stalling?
questions.explain: About six inches of water reaches the underside of most cars and can cause stalling and loss of control; a foot of water floats many cars.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Floods'

questions.q: You come to a road covered with water. What is the safest action?
options: Turn around and find another route
Drive through quickly to avoid stalling
Drive through slowly in low gear
questions.explain: Water can hide a washed-out road. 'Turn Around Don't Drown®'—choose another route. If your vehicle stalls in floodwater, get out and move to higher ground.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Floods'

questions.q: Driving around a barricade or ignoring a warning sign placed where water is over the road is:
options: Legal if your vehicle is high enough
A Class B misdemeanor, with a fine of up to $2,000 and/or up to 180 days in jail
questions.explain: Normally disobeying a warning sign or barricade is a $1–$200 misdemeanor, but where water is over the road it becomes a Class B misdemeanor.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 5: Signals, Signs, and Markers, section 'Obey Warning Signs and Barricades'

questions.q: According to the handbook, if a driver reacts just half a second slower because of a distraction, crashes:
questions.explain: If drivers react a half-second slower because of distractions, crashes double.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Distracted driving'

questions.q: Which of these helps prevent carbon monoxide poisoning?
options: Follow closely behind other cars with vents open
Never leave the motor running in a closed garage
Use the heater in a parked car in an enclosed space
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide is deadly. Don't run the motor in a garage, don't idle with windows closed, and keep your exhaust system in good repair.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'Carbon Monoxide'

questions.q: When a law enforcement officer stops you, you should:
options: Drive to the next exit before stopping, no matter how far
Pull safely to the right, stay in the car, and keep your hands visible on the steering wheel
Get out and walk to the officer's car
Search the glove box for your documents as the officer approaches
questions.explain: Pull over to the right, turn off the engine, turn on hazard lights (and the dome light at night), stay in the vehicle, and keep your hands visible.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'When Stopped by Law Enforcement'

questions.q: When one vehicle tows another with a chain or rope, the connection may be no longer than:
options: 15 feet, with a white flag at least 12 inches square attached
questions.explain: A tow connection may not be longer than 15 feet and must have a white flag at least 12 inches square.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'Towing'

questions.q: What is the minimum legal tire tread depth for vehicles in Texas?
questions.explain: Tires must be in safe condition with at least 2/32 of an inch of tread.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration, section 'Required Equipment for Vehicles'

questions.q: A load or object on your car may not extend more than how far beyond the left side of the body?
questions.explain: The limit is 3 inches past the left side and 6 inches past the right side of the car's body, fenders or running board.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration, section 'Equipment You Must Not Have'

questions.q: If another driver is weaving, driving at inconsistent speeds, or appears to be using a phone, you should:
options: Pass closely to get ahead quickly
Follow closely to signal your annoyance
Give the driver plenty of room and keep a safe following distance
questions.explain: Recognize distracted drivers, give them plenty of room, and be careful when passing—they may drift in front of you.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Distracted driving'

questions.q: To avoid road rage, you should:
options: Tailgate drivers who cut you off
Brake suddenly to warn a tailgater
Speed up to keep others from merging
Tap the horn rather than holding it, and never confront other drivers
questions.explain: Plan ahead, stay calm, tap the horn instead of holding it, don't tailgate, and don't speed up or brake to block others.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'Tips to Avoid Road Rage'

questions.q: If you are tired or not feeling well, you should:
options: Drive with the windows closed and the heater on
Drink coffee and drive the usual way
Drive faster to get home sooner
questions.explain: Adjust to your physical condition; if you are tired or not feeling well, do not drive.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits, section 'Speed'

questions.q: In Texas, a driver 21 or older is legally intoxicated with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explain: A person 21 or older is legally intoxicated at a BAC of 0.08 or more—or at any level that causes loss of normal use of mental or physical faculties.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Know Your Legal Limit'

questions.q: Under Texas's zero tolerance law, a driver under 21 commits an offense if driving with:
questions.explain: A minor with any detectable amount of alcohol while operating a motor vehicle in a public place commits Driving Under the Influence by a Minor.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Zero Tolerance for Minors'

questions.q: Can a driver be considered intoxicated in Texas with a BAC below 0.08?
options: Yes, if alcohol or drugs cause the loss of normal use of mental or physical faculties
Only if the driver is over 65
questions.explain: The legal limit is 0.08 BAC or any amount that results in the loss of normal use of mental or physical faculties.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Know Your Legal Limit'

questions.q: What is the BAC limit for a person driving a commercial motor vehicle?
questions.explain: Commercial drivers have a stricter limit of 0.04 BAC while operating a commercial motor vehicle (federal rule, also in the Texas CDL handbook). The Class C handbook does not cover this.
questions.ref: Texas Commercial Motor Vehicle Drivers Handbook (DL-7C) / 49 CFR 382.201; not covered in DL-7

questions.q: What is the penalty for a first offense of Driving Under the Influence of alcohol by a minor (any detectable amount)?
options: Class C misdemeanor: fine up to $500, 20–40 hours of community service, and an alcohol awareness course
Class A misdemeanor with one year in jail
A $50 fine with no other penalties
questions.explain: A minor's first DUI is a Class C misdemeanor with a fine up to $500, 20 to 40 hours of community service, and a required alcohol awareness course.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 29: Penalties for Driving Under the Influence (DUI) of Alcohol and Drugs – Minors'

questions.q: A driver under 21 refuses to give a breath or blood specimen for the first time. The license is suspended for:
questions.explain: A minor's first refusal brings a 180-day suspension; a second or later refusal brings 2 years.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Implied Consent Laws for Minors'

questions.q: A minor's breath test shows a detectable amount of alcohol below 0.08. On a first offense, the license is suspended for:
questions.explain: For a minor whose specimen shows a detectable amount of alcohol: 60 days (1st), 120 days (2nd), 180 days (3rd and later).
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Implied Consent Laws for Minors'

questions.q: An adult driver refuses a breath or blood test after a DWI arrest. For a first refusal, the license is suspended for:
questions.explain: Refusing a specimen results in a 180-day suspension, or up to 730 days for later offenses.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Implied Consent Laws for Adults'

questions.q: An adult driver submits to a test that shows a BAC of 0.08 or more (first offense). Under administrative license revocation, the license may be suspended for:
questions.explain: A test result of 0.08 or more brings a 90-day suspension, or up to 365 days for later offenses.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Implied Consent Laws for Adults'

questions.q: What does Texas's implied consent law mean?
options: By driving, you have agreed to give a breath or blood specimen if lawfully arrested for DWI
Police need your written permission to test you
You may refuse a test with no penalty
Only drivers under 21 can be tested
questions.explain: Drivers are considered to have consented to breath or blood testing if arrested for driving while intoxicated; refusing leads to suspension.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Implied Consent Laws for Adults'; Appendix A: Glossary, 'implied-consent law'

questions.q: What is the reinstatement fee after an Administrative License Revocation (ALR) suspension?
questions.explain: A $125 reinstatement fee is required for all ALR suspensions.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Administrative License Revocation (ALR)'

questions.q: For an adult's first DWI conviction, the maximum fine is:
questions.explain: A first DWI carries a fine of up to $2,000, 72 hours to 180 days in jail, and a 90-day to 365-day license suspension.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 31: Penalties for DWI and DUI of Alcohol or Drugs – Adults'

questions.q: A first DWI conviction can bring jail time of:
questions.explain: A first DWI is punishable by 72 hours to 180 days in jail.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 31: Penalties for DWI and DUI of Alcohol or Drugs – Adults'

questions.q: If a driver convicted of a first DWI also had an open container of alcohol, the minimum jail time increases to:
questions.explain: Possession of an open container of an alcoholic beverage increases the minimum confinement for a first DWI to six days.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 30: Penalties for Driving While Intoxicated (Alcohol)'

questions.q: A second DWI conviction is punishable by:
options: A fine up to $4,000 and 30 days to 1 year in jail
A fine up to $2,000 and 72 hours in jail
questions.explain: A second DWI brings a fine up to $4,000, 30 days to 1 year in jail, and a 180-day to 2-year license suspension.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 31: Penalties for DWI and DUI of Alcohol or Drugs – Adults'

questions.q: A third DWI conviction in Texas is:
options: A felony punishable by 2 to 10 years in prison and a fine up to $10,000
questions.explain: A third or later DWI is a third-degree felony: 2 to 10 years in the Texas Department of Criminal Justice and up to $10,000.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 31: Penalties for DWI and DUI of Alcohol or Drugs – Adults'

questions.q: Driving while intoxicated with a passenger younger than 15 is:
options: The same as a regular first DWI
questions.explain: DWI with a passenger under 15 is a state jail felony punishable by 180 days to 2 years and a fine up to $10,000.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 31: Penalties for DWI and DUI of Alcohol or Drugs – Adults'

questions.q: Intoxication manslaughter (causing a death while intoxicated) is punishable by:
options: 2 to 20 years in prison and a fine up to $10,000
questions.explain: Intoxication manslaughter is a second-degree felony with 2 to 20 years in prison and a fine up to $10,000.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 31: Penalties for DWI and DUI of Alcohol or Drugs – Adults'

questions.q: Is it legal to have an open container of alcohol in the passenger area of a car parked on a public highway?
options: No; it is illegal whether the car is moving, stopped or parked, with a fine up to $500
Yes, if the car is parked
Yes, if the container is less than half full
questions.explain: Possessing an open container in a vehicle's passenger area on a public highway is illegal whether the vehicle is operated, stopped, or parked.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Open Container'

questions.q: What is the only thing that sobers up a person who has been drinking?
questions.explain: Coffee, cold showers and exercise do not work. Only time—about one hour per drink—reduces the effects of alcohol.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Myths about Drinking Alcohol'

questions.q: About how long does it take the body to get rid of the alcohol in one drink?
questions.explain: It takes about one hour for the body to rid itself of each drink.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Myths about Drinking Alcohol'

questions.q: Which contains about the same amount of alcohol as a 12-ounce can of beer?
questions.explain: A 12-ounce beer, a 5-ounce glass of wine, and a mixed drink with 1.5 ounces of liquor all contain about the same amount of alcohol.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 32: Alcohol and Driving. Why Take the Risk?'

questions.q: A minor's first conviction for a non-driving alcohol offense (such as possession) results in a license suspension of:
questions.explain: A first non-driving alcohol offense by a minor brings a fine up to $500, 8–12 hours of community service, an alcohol awareness course, and a 30-day suspension.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Penalties for Non-Driving Alcohol-Related Offenses by Minors'

questions.q: An adult who buys alcohol for, or gives alcohol to, a minor faces:
options: A warning on the first offense
A fine of up to $4,000 and/or up to one year in jail
questions.explain: Purchasing, furnishing, or selling alcohol to a minor is punishable by a fine up to $4,000 and/or up to one year in jail.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 1: Your License to Drive, section 'Other Non-Driving Penalties for Alcohol-Related Offenses'

questions.q: One of the first effects of alcohol on a driver is:
questions.explain: Alcohol, a depressant, first affects judgment and vision, slowing reactions and the ability to judge other vehicles' speed.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Chapter 10 introduction'

questions.q: Why is it dangerous to combine alcohol with tranquilizers or sedatives?
options: It is only dangerous for drivers under 21
questions.explain: Alcohol increases the depressant effects of tranquilizers and barbiturates; mixing drugs can be very hazardous.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 25: Alcohol and Other Types of Drugs'

questions.q: Before driving after taking an over-the-counter cold medicine or antihistamine, you should:
options: Drink coffee to cancel the effect
Read the label, because many cause drowsiness
Take a double dose to feel better quickly
questions.explain: Many over-the-counter drugs cause drowsiness. Read labels and ask a doctor or pharmacist if unsure.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 25: Alcohol and Other Types of Drugs'

questions.q: How does marijuana affect driving?
options: It has no effect on driving
Even typical doses can impair concentration, judgment and perception
questions.explain: Research shows even typical social doses of marijuana can affect the concentration, judgment and perceptual skills needed for driving.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 10: Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability, section 'Table 25: Alcohol and Other Types of Drugs'

questions.q: You are in a crash in which someone is injured. You must:
options: Stop only if the crash was your fault
Leave and call police from home
Stop at or near the scene, exchange information, and give reasonable help to the injured
Move all injured people into your car
questions.explain: Stop immediately at or as close as possible to the scene, give your name, address, registration and insurer, show your license if asked, and provide reasonable assistance.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes, section 'Crash Resulting in Injury to, or Death of a person'

questions.q: After a crash involving another driver, what information should you provide?
options: Your name and address, vehicle registration number, and liability insurer
questions.explain: Give your name, address, vehicle registration number and the name of your liability insurer, and show your driver license if requested.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes, section 'Crash Resulting in Injury to, or Death of a person'

questions.q: You have a minor crash on a freeway main lane. No one is hurt and both cars can be driven safely. You should:
options: Move the vehicles off the main lanes to a safe nearby location
Stand between the cars to direct traffic
Leave the cars where they are until police arrive
questions.explain: If each vehicle can be driven safely, move it as soon as possible to a crash investigation site, the frontage road, a nearby cross street, or another safe spot.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes, section 'Crash Resulting in Damage to a Vehicle'

questions.q: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. You must:
options: Report it only if the damage is over $1,000
Drive away; it was parked illegally
Leave a note in a visible place with your name, address, and an explanation of what happened
questions.explain: Stop and either locate the owner or securely attach a written notice with your name, address, and the circumstances of the collision.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes, section 'Crash Involving an Unattended Vehicle'

questions.q: In which situation should you notify law enforcement about a crash as soon as possible?
options: When the other driver offers to pay cash
Only when the crash is on a freeway
When someone is injured or killed
Only when your car cannot be driven
questions.explain: Notify law enforcement when there is an injury or fatality, the vehicles cannot be moved, a driver leaves the scene, or you suspect a driver is intoxicated.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes, section 'Chapter 11 introduction'

questions.q: Leaving the scene of a crash that caused someone's death (failure to stop and render aid) is:
options: A second-degree felony punishable by 2 to 20 years in prison
questions.explain: Failure to stop in a crash resulting in death is a second-degree felony with a fine up to $10,000 and 2 to 20 years in prison.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes, section 'Table 33: Penalties for Failure to Stop'

questions.q: Failing to stop after damaging an attended vehicle, with less than $200 in damage, is:
options: A Class C misdemeanor with a fine up to $500
questions.explain: With less than $200 in damage it is a Class C misdemeanor; with $200 or more it is a Class B misdemeanor.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes, section 'Table 34: Penalties for Failure to Stop'

questions.q: You are the victim of a hit-and-run crash. What should you do?
options: Do nothing, since you can't find the other driver
Wait to see if the other driver calls you
Report it only to your mechanic
questions.explain: Report hit-and-run crashes to law enforcement. Uninsured motorist coverage pays for hit-and-run damage only when it has been reported.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes, section 'Hit-and-Run Crashes'

questions.q: When helping someone injured in a crash, you should:
options: Give the person something to drink
Move the person to your car right away
Not move the injured person unless it is absolutely necessary
Help the person stand up and walk around
questions.explain: Send for skilled help. Do not move or lift victims unless absolutely necessary, and keep them comfortable.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes, section 'Aiding the Injured'

questions.q: How should you try to control serious bleeding while waiting for help?
options: Raise the person to a standing position
Press thick, clean cloth pads firmly on the wound
questions.explain: Stop serious bleeding by applying pressure with thick, clean cloth pads, by hand or with a bandage.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes, section 'Aiding the Injured'

questions.q: Your car stalls on railroad tracks and a train is coming. You should:
options: Run along the tracks away from the train
Get everyone out and move away from the tracks toward the direction the train is coming from
Get out and stand beside the car
Stay in the car and try to restart it
questions.explain: Get out quickly and move away from the tracks, going toward the approaching train (off to the side) to avoid flying debris.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Additional Safe Driving Procedures at Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: The blue and white Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign at a railroad crossing is used to:
options: Call the railroad about an emergency or a signal problem, giving the crossing's ID number
Mark a quiet zone where trains don't sound horns
Tell drivers to stop at all times
questions.explain: The ENS sign lists the railroad's emergency number and the USDOT crossing number, which identifies the exact location of the crossing.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Highway-Rail Grade Crossings Emergency Notification System (ENS)'

questions.q: Your car breaks down and you cannot get it completely off the road. What should you do?
options: Stay inside with the doors locked and wait
Stand behind the car to wave traffic around
Leave the lights off to save the battery
Get everyone out of the car and away from the road, and warn oncoming traffic
questions.explain: If you can't get the car off the road, get everyone out and off the road and use warning devices to alert traffic.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Vehicle Breakdown'

questions.q: To signal that your stopped vehicle needs help, you can:
options: Turn on your hazard lights and tie a white cloth to the antenna or door handle, or raise the hood
questions.explain: Turn on emergency flashers and tie a white cloth where it can be seen; if you have no cloth, raise the hood.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Vehicle Breakdown'

questions.q: You are driving in a roundabout when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren on. You should:
options: Continue to your exit, leave the circle, and then pull over
Speed up to stay ahead of it in the circle
questions.explain: Do not stop inside the roundabout. Clear the circle first, then pull over for the emergency vehicle.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: An unmarked car signals you to stop at night on a dark road, and you are unsure it is a real police vehicle. What does the handbook say you may do?
options: Ignore the signal and keep driving normally
Turn on your hazard lights, drive slowly, call 9-1-1, and stop at a nearby well-lit, populated place
Stop in a travel lane and get out
questions.explain: You may turn on hazards, drive slowly below the limit, call 9-1-1 to verify, and go to a nearby well-lit, populated place to stop.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'Obligations, Responsibilities, Courtesy and Safety'

questions.q: You find someone overcome by carbon monoxide in a car. What should you do?
options: Let the person sleep it off in the car
Move the person to fresh air and call 911
questions.explain: Move a carbon monoxide victim into fresh air and call 911.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips, section 'Carbon Monoxide'

questions.q: You notice a railroad crossing signal is not working properly. Whom can you call?
options: No one; railroads check them daily
The DPS Communications Center or local police or sheriff, giving the crossing's ID number
The Texas Department of Motor Vehicles title office
questions.explain: Report signal problems to DPS at (800) 772-7677 or to local police or the sheriff, and give the crossing signal's identification number.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 4: Right-of-Way, section 'Additional Safe Driving Procedures at Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: If your vehicle stalls in floodwater, you should:
options: Get out quickly and move to higher ground
Try to push the car through the water
Stay inside and wait for the water to go down
questions.explain: National Weather Service and state officials advise getting out quickly and moving to higher ground if your vehicle stalls in floodwater.
questions.ref: Texas Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. January 2026), Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations, section 'Floods'
